judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures hold. Every one of the ten problems prints a Step/Reason (or Legal?/Reason) table whose Reason column the student must fill, the directions say "Fill in the Reason column of each table as you go", and the reason bank names the five properties to be used - yet verify.json contains only `solve`, `eval`, `equiv` and `inequality` entries against terminal values, and gate_log.txt reports "12 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual". The six open diagnoses are real: problem 3 ("explain in one sentence why this rewriting never changes an equation's solutions"), 4 ("Find the first line that is not legal, say what she did instead"), 5 ("state clearly what happens to the inequality symbol and why"), 7 ("explain exactly which condition fails here"), 8 ("say whether the two equations are equivalent"), 10 ("Name the line, name the property it should have used"). I also confirmed all ten keyed values independently (x=5 with check 22, x=32, 2x+10, x=3 with check 12, x>-4, x=13, roots 0 and 4, 2(-1)+6=4, x<=-1, x=7). Where I part company: the judge cleared the print quality - "The reason tables and model solutions render cleanly" - and the answer key's Quick Answers bank does not. Entry 5 prints "-4, [infinity], <built-in function open>" and entry 9 prints "-[infinity], -1, loopen". scripts/render_quick_answers.py `_fmt` sympifies each element of the interval triple; sympy.sympify("open") resolves to Python's builtin `open` and sympy.latex renders it as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. A Python object repr is printed on page 1 of a teacher-facing answer key.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is the best-engineered item on the sheet: Ravi's illegal "divide by 2" is made checkable by having the student substitute Ravi's solution back into the ORIGINAL left side (2(-1)+6 = 4 against a right side of 10), and the declared trap value 5 captures the exact wrong move of substituting into the changed equation instead. That is how an equivalence-judging task becomes machine-checkable without faking the reasoning half.

The key opens with the grader instruction the topic actually needs: "Credit the reason, not just the arithmetic: a student who reaches the right number while writing 'subtracted 7' on a line where 7 was subtracted from one side only has not yet learned this skill."

Problem 7 (x^2 = 4x divided by x) puts the division-by-a-variable condition in front of an Algebra 1 student without needing any later course, and the key's solution names the lost root explicitly rather than only listing {0, 4}.
The reason bank at the top lists the five property names with no values filled in, so the vocabulary is supplied without leaking any problem's answer.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 257 already says it plainly - "Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer" - but line 249 immediately narrows it ("Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning") and tells the author to reframe error analysis "via the ordinary types". Read together, the guidance reads as a licence to type an explanation-bearing problem by its numeric half. Nothing in the gate chain notices, because no gate reads the problem prose looking for a demanded explanation. On this sheet the effect is total: the named subject of the worksheet is the REASON for each step, and not one reason is inside the trust boundary.
evidence: worksheet directions: "Fill in the Reason column of each table as you go"
all ten problems print a Step/Reason or Legal?/Reason table with blank Reason cells
verify.json holds only solve/eval/equiv/inequality entries and no manual entry
worksheet problems 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10 each demand a written diagnosis in the stem

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py `_fmt` routes every string through sympy.sympify, which is wrong for the openness token of an `inequality` expected triple. sympify("open") returns Python's builtin `open` function and sympy.latex renders it as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}; "loopen", "closed" and "hiopen" fall through as bare symbols. Beyond the object repr, the bank prints the raw JSON triple instead of the interval or inequality a grader wants. This is the same defect family as the known quick-answer-bank-drops-relation-answers bug - one unguarded sympify over a non-expression string - with a worse output.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: "5. -4, [infinity], <built-in function open>" and "9. -[infinity], -1, loopen"
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): the isinstance(v, str) branch calls sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)) with no token guard

root_causes.description: SKILL.md's verification contract has a per-PROBLEM floor, not a per-RESPONSE-SLOT floor: "verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check". A multi-part sheet therefore satisfies the gate with one scalar per id, and build.sh prints "0 manual" - which reads as "everything on this sheet was checked" rather than "every id had something checked". Problem 8 shows it concretely: its table has two cells to fill (the solution of x+6=5, and the value of 2x+6 there) and only the second is checked.
evidence: worksheet problem 8 table rows: "x+6=5 | Its solution" and "value of 2x+6 there"
verify.json id 8: a single eval entry (2*x+6 at x=-1 -> 4); nothing checks that x+6=5 solves to -1
worksheet problem 1 by contrast carries two entries (solve x=5 and eval 3x+7=22), so the multi-entry pattern exists in the same file

improvements.title: Reason columns and step diagnoses must be declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so that a filled-in Reason column, a named property, or a "which line is illegal and why" diagnosis is declared as a `manual` entry alongside the id's numeric check, and add the prose lint in tests/check_layout.py described for this cluster (stems containing "explain", "name the property", "say what", "state clearly", "which condition fails"). Here that is one manual entry per problem for the Reason column plus explicit diagnosis entries on ids 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 10; every desc already exists as prose in answer_key.pdf.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints a Step/Reason table and a stem saying "name the reason for each line", with a verify JSON holding only a solve entry. Assert the build exits 2 and lists problem 1 as manual. Today it exits 0 with "0 manual".
improvements.expected_impact: The subject the sheet actually assesses - legal transformations and their justifications - moves inside the declared review boundary; the manual count goes from 0 to at least 6, and the delivery text stops describing a reasoning worksheet as fully machine-checked.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over problem prose will fire on stems that use "explain" inside a hint rather than as a demand. Ship it as exit 2 (manual-review visibility), which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: Quick Answers prints "<built-in function open>" for inequality answers
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle the `inequality` expected triple as a unit before any element reaches sympify: render [lo, hi, openness] as interval notation with the bracket style taken from the openness token (open -> (lo, hi), closed -> [lo, hi], loopen -> (lo, hi], hiopen -> [lo, hi)), mapping "oo"/"-oo" to \infty and forcing an open bracket on any infinite end. Additionally guard `_fmt` so a string that sympifies to anything other than a sympy Expr (functions, builtins, booleans) falls back rather than being latex-printed - sympify("open") returning Python's builtin is the general hazard, not a one-token special case.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py rendering {"id": 1, "type": "inequality", "expr": "-2*x-8", "relation": "<", "expected": [-4, "oo", "open"]} and asserting the bank line for id 1 contains "(-4, \infty)" and does NOT contain "built-in function". It fails today, printing the Python object repr.
improvements.expected_impact: Every worksheet whose verification_targets include `inequality` gets a readable, correct bank entry instead of a raw JSON triple, and the object-repr leak - which unambiguously destroys trust in the document it appears on - disappears.
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank, which is plain text and is never read by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate cannot be affected. The compile-ak gate catches any bad LaTeX spelling immediately.

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule in SKILL.md from "every id 1..N has at least one check" to "every printed response slot has a check", and enforce it mechanically: add a slot counter to tests/check_layout.py (which already parses the worksheet .tex for answer-location macros) that counts, per problem, the lettered parts ((a)/(b)/(c)), the blank cells of a fill-in table, and each answer line, then reports when a problem's verify entries number fewer than its slots. Multi-entry ids are already legal and already used in these same files, so the fix adds entries, not machinery.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 2 prints "(a) ... (b) ... (c) ..." with a verify JSON holding a single eval entry for id 2. Assert the gate chain flags problem 2 with the two uncovered parts named. Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims full verification.
improvements.expected_impact: Multi-part problems stop being certified on the strength of their last line. Across this batch the same shape appears in curr-252, curr-256, curr-275, curr-276 and curr-300.
improvements.risk: Medium: counting slots from .tex will over-count where a lettered part is rhetorical rather than a response. Ship as exit 2 (manual visibility) before promoting to exit 1, so a correct build is never blocked by a parse artefact.

case_summary: Pedagogically this is one of the strongest sheets in my batch: a reason bank, a Step/Reason table on every problem, an equivalence test built by substituting back into the ORIGINAL side (problem 8), the divide-by-a-variable condition (problem 7), and a key that tells the grader to credit the reason rather than the number. All ten values check out under independent solution. It is rejected because the reasons - the literal subject of the worksheet - are outside verification and the build reports "0 manual". Two findings the judge did not raise: the Quick Answers bank prints "<built-in function open>" for problem 5 and "loopen" for problem 9, a sympify leak in render_quick_answers.py that puts a Python object repr on page 1 of the answer key (the judge explicitly cleared print quality); and problem 8's table has two cells to fill with only the second checked.
